newsitem.title: USA: CHINA WHEAT UP 7 MLN TONNES, OILSEEDS DOWN - USDA.
newsitem.headline: CHINA WHEAT UP 7 MLN TONNES, OILSEEDS DOWN - USDA.

text.p: China will reap 121 million tonnes of wheat, seven million more than forecast a month ago, but its oilseed output is slipping, U.S. Agriculture Department estimated Tuesday.
"China's wheat crop is up seven million tonnes from last month and more than 10 million above last year," USDA said in its monthly World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates report.
USDA said peanut and soybean production was down.

"Dry weather in the North China Plain hurt peanut yields while soybean yields will be mainly determined by August weather. Soybean area in China is reduced based on a smaller shift in grain area to soybeans than previously anticipated," USDA said. "China is forecast to increase its imports of soybeans and products along with palm oil to meet rapidly growing demand for protein meal and vegetable oil."

Chinese wheat imports were forecast for 2.5 million tonnes, down one million tonnes from one month ago. Its corn crop was estimated at 110 million tonnes, 12 million less than in July. Corn exports were placed at one million tonnes, half of the July forecast.
Soybean production in China was forecast for 13.5 million tonnes, down one million from last month. Imports were boosted to 2.75 million tonnes, compared to 2.25 million in July.
Soymeal imports by China were placed at 3.35 million tonnes, up 350,000 tonnes from July, and soyoil imports were forecast for 1.60 million tonnes, up from July's 1.55 million tonnes.
